feed.title: Standardizing public key exposure classification for existing outputs

entry.title: Standardizing public key exposure classification for existing outputs
entry.summary:
The recent updates to the Bitcoin Improvement Proposal (BIP) draft, now at version 0.5.1, have been submitted for consideration as an Informational BIP in the BIPs repository. The current draft incorporates significant revisions following a review, notably addressing vulnerabilities related to the exposure classifications within Bitcoin transactions. Specifically, the first two levels of exposure are now aligned with the taxonomy outlined in BIP 360, detailing long and short exposure per output, which strengthens the clarity and application of these classifications.
Furthermore, a correction has been made concerning the exposure status of P2MR transactions. Contrary to previous assertions, it is now clarified that a leaf spend under P2MR involves exposing the leaf script, its Merkle path, and a secp256k1 key within the mempool. This revelation aligns P2MR with the exposure characteristics of P2WSH, correcting the earlier misclassification and adjusting the exposure status to EXPOSED_ON_SPEND until solutions that can withstand post-quantum threats are developed. Currently, no transaction type falls under the NOT_EXPOSED category, indicating a gap that might need addressing in future proposals.
The draft, along with the reference implementation and 25 vectors, is accessible for review and feedback at [this GitHub link](https://github.com/duncan0k/pubkey-exposure-classification). Stakeholder feedback is crucial for the progression of this BIP, and contributors are encouraged to share their insights directly on the pull request to influence the final outcome effectively.
